text:
Both assistants provide accurate, accessible explanations of language models and correctly identify that they are trained on unlabeled data. However, Assistant B edges out slightly due to its inclusion of concrete real-world examples (voice assistants, machine translation, predictive text) that help non-technical customers connect the concept to familiar applications, its explicit clarification that models "only require unlabelled data — just lots of plain text," and its customer-service-oriented closing that invites follow-up questions. Assistant A is clear and correct but lacks these trust-building, application-focused details.

[[B]]
